$comment: Reading order and layer grouping for the corpus. Derived from the corpus README's own five-layer framing — NOT alphabetical. `docs` are content collection ids (path under content/, without .md). Every markdown file under content/ must appear exactly once here; scripts/extract-meta.mjs fails the build otherwise.

layers.title: Getting Started
layers.blurb: The only document here that assumes you have never been on the ice: how to find a session, what registration involves, which tier you belong in, and what actually happens in your first hour at the rink.

layers.title: Foundation
layers.blurb: What everything is called, what is legal, and the words you shout. The canonical references the rest of the corpus links back to.

layers.title: Positions
layers.tagline: Where do I stand and what is my job?
layers.blurb: The four positions, plus the bridge between them. The three skater documents share one skeleton — by zone, then by situation within each zone. The goaltender document deliberately does not.

layers.title: Systems and Situations
layers.tagline: How five players act as one
layers.blurb: Team structure in every zone and every situation. Where a system determines your job, the system is named and an alternative is given — because most breakdowns are two players working from different assumptions.

layers.title: Technique
layers.tagline: How do I physically execute it?
layers.blurb: The physical skills every other layer is performed on top of.

layers.title: Hockey IQ
layers.tagline: How do I read the play and decide?
layers.blurb: Support, space, scanning and risk. Knowing your position and the systems without this means executing the wrong thing at the right time.

layers.title: Off the Ice
layers.blurb: Not a layer of play, but every layer above depends on it: kit, conditioning, practice, the mental side, culture, and how to watch.
